title: RBH17 5-round AES-128 / aes128-5r-yoyo-key-recovery-rbh2017

target.description: 5 nonlinear AES rounds in the source enck/deck convention, omitting initial ShiftRows and final ShiftRows/MixColumns. Section 3 explains public linear conjugation to full-round AES. Recovers all four 32-bit words of the 128-bit whitening key; this is the AES-128 master key. The four words called subkeys in Section 3.5 are not four complete round keys.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key and its expanded round keys.
setting.plaintext_model: Yoyo swap-generated adaptive encryption/decryption texts under one unknown key; the source native chosen-text count is not automatically an aggregate oracle-call count.
setting.reference_model: Complete recovery of the128-bit initial whitening/master key of five-round AES128 under adaptive bidirectional unknown-key access; this is not a random-permutation distinguishing experiment.

time.note: Source counts about 2^37.3 S-box lookups, divides by 5*16; remaining whitening words are included at lower order. Source leading2^37.3219S-box lookups divided by80lookups per five-round AES gives2^31; residual subkeys called negligible. This is not wall-clock runtime.

data.note: Section 3.5 final total includes remaining-word recovery; native texts/pairs, not an independently normalized total of all oracle calls. The total is 2560 native texts (log2 approximately 11.3219), from 2 × 256 × 5. Original/prose pair choices and aggregate encryption/decryption queries remain distinct.

success.description: First 32-bit-word false positive is estimated at 2^-16 with five test pairs; four/five more pairs resolve the other words. Source gives no numerical whole-master-key success.

review.scope: Checked Section3.5 and Algorithm6: useful-pair existence and first-word filter estimates do not quantify complete master-key recovery. The existing five-returned-versus-five-total-pairs conflict remains.

components.description: The Section3.5 prose estimates five independent returned-pair filters for one wrong first-word candidate. Algorithm6 includes the initial pair among five total pairs; the existing source conflict applies to this estimate.

Source estimate over 2^24 first-word candidates using the prose five-returned-pair argument. This is a local false-positive estimate, not complete-master-key recovery success; the pair-count conflict remains.
